questions.q: Which of these elements has the largest atomic radius?
questions.e: Radius increases down a group; among these, Cs is lowest in the group.

questions.q: What is the ground-state electron configuration of Fe²⁺?
questions.e: Transition metals lose 4s electrons before 3d electrons: Fe is [Ar]4s²3d⁶, so Fe²⁺ is [Ar]3d⁶.

questions.q: Why is the first ionization energy of oxygen lower than that of nitrogen?
c: Pairing in one 2p orbital of O introduces electron–electron repulsion that eases removal of that electron
Oxygen has a larger atomic radius than nitrogen
Oxygen has a lower effective nuclear charge than nitrogen
Nitrogen has a filled 2s subshell and oxygen does not
questions.e: N has three unpaired 2p electrons; O has one paired 2p electron whose repulsion makes it easier to remove, despite O's higher Zeff.

questions.q: Explain why chromium is [Ar]3d⁵4s¹ rather than [Ar]3d⁴4s².
questions.m: The 3d and 4s subshells are very close in energy. Moving one electron into 3d gives a half-filled d subshell (five parallel-spin electrons), which maximizes exchange energy and reduces electron–electron repulsion, outweighing the small cost of promoting a 4s electron.

questions.q: What is the molecular geometry of H₂O?
questions.e: Four electron domains (two bonding, two lone pairs) give tetrahedral electron geometry and a bent molecular shape.

questions.q: What is the molecular geometry of XeF₄?
questions.e: Six electron domains (octahedral): four bonds and two lone pairs trans to each other, giving square planar.

questions.q: Which species has the smallest bond angle?
questions.e: Approximate angles: BF₃ 120°, CH₄ 109.5°, NH₃ about 107°, H₂O about 104.5°. More lone-pair repulsion compresses the angle.

questions.q: Predict the electron geometry, molecular geometry, hybridization and polarity of SF₄.
questions.m: Five electron domains (four S–F bonds + one lone pair): trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry, see-saw molecular geometry (lone pair equatorial), sp³d hybridization, and polar because the bond dipoles do not cancel.

questions.q: How many moles are in 36.0 g of H₂O (M = 18.0 g/mol)?
For 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, starting with 4.0 mol H₂ and 3.0 mol O₂, what is the maximum amount of H₂O formed?
questions.e: 4.0 mol H₂ needs only 2.0 mol O₂, so H₂ is limiting and gives 4.0 mol H₂O.

questions.q: A compound is 40.0% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O by mass. Its empirical formula is:
questions.e: Per 100 g: 3.33 mol C, 6.6 mol H, 3.33 mol O → ratio 1 : 2 : 1.

questions.q: What volume of 0.0500 M NaOH neutralizes 25.0 mL of 0.100 M HCl?
Approximately what volume does 1.00 mol of an ideal gas occupy at 0 °C and 1 atm?
For a process at constant pressure that releases heat to the surroundings, which statement is correct?
c: ΔH is negative and equals q_P
ΔH is positive and equals q_P
questions.e: At constant pressure ΔH = q_P; heat released means q_P < 0, so ΔH < 0 (exothermic).

questions.q: In the van der Waals equation, what do the parameters a and b account for?
questions.m: a corrects for attractive intermolecular forces (lowering the pressure relative to ideal: P + a n²/V²), and b corrects for the finite volume of the molecules (reducing the free volume: V − nb).

questions.q: What is the pH of 1.0 × 10⁻³ M HCl?
questions.e: HCl is a strong acid, so [H⁺] = 1.0×10⁻³ M and pH = 3.0.

questions.q: For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (ΔH < 0), raising the temperature at constant pressure will:
c: Shift the equilibrium toward reactants and lower K
Shift toward products and raise K
Not change K but speed up equilibrium
Shift toward products but leave K unchanged
questions.e: Heat is a product of an exothermic reaction; adding heat shifts the equilibrium left, and K decreases.

questions.q: What is the approximate pH of 0.10 M of a weak acid with Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵?
What is the oxidation state of Mn in KMnO₄?
questions.e: K is +1 and four O are −2 each: +1 + x − 8 = 0, so x = +7.

questions.q: Given E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V and E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V, what is E°cell for the galvanic cell Zn | Zn²⁺ || Cu²⁺ | Cu?
Write the relationships linking ΔG°, K and E°cell, and state what a positive E° implies.
questions.m: ΔG° = −nFE° = −RT ln K (equivalently E° = (RT/nF) ln K = (0.0592/n) log K at 25 °C). A positive E° means ΔG° < 0 and K > 1: the reaction is spontaneous under standard conditions.
